name: Institut Laue-Langevin
notes: Created by the cevns workstream (ID_REGISTRY Wave 3) as the host facility of the Ricochet experiment.

ILL is primarily a multinational neutron-science user facility; it is recorded here with kind:reactor_site because the property relevant to Ricochet's CEvNS program is its 58.3 MW research reactor core, the same kind used for the other cevns-workstream reactor facilities (Brokdorf, Leibstadt).

operator.note: Not independently confirmed against ILL's own official page in this pass.
operator.value: Institut Laue-Langevin (a tripartite French-German-British research organisation)

summary.plain: A major research reactor in Grenoble, France, mainly used to make beams of neutrons for science, and also home to the Ricochet reactor-neutrino experiment.
summary.technical: Institut Laue-Langevin (ILL), Grenoble, France: 58.3 MW research reactor (Wikipedia) / 58 MW per Ricochet's own background paper; hosts the Ricochet CEvNS experiment 8.8 m from the reactor core. Reactor thermal power is not recorded as a `specs` quantity because the only Appendix A power-dimension key, `beam_power`, has an A21 plausibility range (1 kW-10 MW) built for accelerator beamlines, not a megawatt-scale research reactor; the figure is given here in prose instead.
